structured.target: Raymart S. Garcia Reskyusi Food Basket Philippine Resilience Awards
structured.theme_or_track: Youth Category; 2025 theme “Kababaihan at Kabataan: Katuwang sa Paghahabi ng Isang Matatag na Bayan”
structured.what_it_does: Barangay food bank and food-rescue facility that collects surplus edible produce from public markets (Wed/Sat nights, 80+ youth volunteers), processes and distributes food baskets to food-insecure families and undernourished children, and routes inedible scraps to community composting and vermicomposting so vermicast returns to local urban gardens—cutting landfill methane while addressing malnutrition.
structured.outcome_or_award: Youth Category Resilience Champion / awardee, Philippine Resilience Awards 2025; barangay also cited with DENR Kwentong KLIMA-likasan; PIA feature also notes Galing Pook and Walang Gutom Awards for the program
structured.gap: Other named co-builders/team leads beyond Raymart S. Garcia not listed in official award write-ups; program founding year not stated on CCC/PIA award pages (PIA feature says it began from a youth-camp idea and is described as the country’s first barangay-established food bank/rescue facility, without a calendar year); PRA Youth Category lists five co-champions with no 1st/2nd ranking published; Galing Pook / Walang Gutom award years and exact placement not verified in the sources fetched for PRA.
structured.note: Strong CCC / Youth CLAP fit: PRA is a CCC multistakeholder program (with PCW, National Resilience Council, SM Prime, WiNDRR, ARISE PH), initiated by Sen. Loren Legarda; ceremony at Philippine Normal University during 18th Global Warming and Climate Change Consciousness Week (late 2025). Garcia is Barangay Commonwealth Kagawad and is quoted as Reskyusi Program Officer. Name “Reskyusi” = rescue + Kyusi (Quezon City). Useful student angle: circular food system (rescue → baskets → compost/vermicast → urban farms) linking food security, waste, and climate.
